newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYBEANS END HIGHER, GAINS CURBED BY BIG CROP.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYBEANS END HIGHER, GAINS CURBED BY BIG CROP.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher Tuesday on strength borrowed from limit gains in corn, but soy advances were clipped by prospects for a record U.S. soybean crop in 1997/98, traders and analysts said.
"With corn at the limit, it has spurred additional interest in the bean market from the speculative community," said Mark Widener, analyst with Cargill Investor Services.
"But the trade realizes that the rains of the past 24 to 48 hours can help us achieve those record yields," he said.
Rain in the U.S. Midwest since Sunday is seen giving the developing soybean crop a big production boost, traders said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast a record soybean crop of 2.744 million bushels, which weighed on new crop contracts throughout the session. That production figure was up 15 percent from last year's crop and higher than trade expectations for 2.607 to 2.731 billion bushels.
August soybeans were sharply higher in response to talk of an ongoing export program off the U.S. Great Lakes and demand for soybeans for export at the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
CBOT soybeans ended steady to 20 cents per bushel higher, with November up 1-1/2 cents at $6.11-1/2 a bushel. August ended up 20 cents per bushel at $7.43-3/4.
Another supportive factor in trade on Tuesday were signs of crop deterioration in the USDA's weekly crop progress report on Monday, traders said.
USDA said 55 percent of the soybean crop as of Sunday was in good to excellent condition, less than 60 percent in that category a week earlier.
However, traders said that much of the damage showing in that report will be reversed by rainfall this week.
On the day, Term Commodities bought three million bushels November and Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought four million November. Refco sold three million November and one million August, pit sources said.
In options trade, Tradelink sold 500 November $6.50 calls, Cargill Investor Services sold 500 November $7.00 calls and Refco bought 400 November $5.25 puts, pit sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 44,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 36,978.
